issue.title: Bootstrap repo: uv project, typer CLI skeleton, ruff, mypy, pytest, pre-commit
issue.body:
# M0-04 — Bootstrap the `vault` repo

Ticket: [#16](https://github.com/stephenkiers/PhotoLibrary/issues/16) · milestone M0 · estimate **S** · `depends_on: []`

## Context

The repo currently holds three files — `issues.json`, `.github-issue-map.json`, and two
program-management scripts under `scripts/`. There is no Python project, no package, no
tests, no lint config, no `.github/` directory. Eighty-six tracked issues build on top of
this ticket; M0-05 (config), M0-06 (hashing), M0-10 (fixtures) and M0-11 (Docker) all list
M0-04 as their only dependency.

The purpose of this ticket is to make the next ticket cheap: a `vault` command whose full
planned surface exists as stubs, a type checker and linter that are strict while the repo is
empty (they are nearly free now and expensive at M0-09), and a push gate that runs on the
Mac. Two acceptance criteria, verbatim from the ticket:

- `uv run vault --help` lists all planned subcommands as stubs
- CI runs lint, type check, tests on push

The repo is **public** already, which raises the cost of the M0-02 secret-leak class of
mistake and makes `.gitignore` + gitleaks load-bearing from commit one.

## Decisions Made

| # | Decision | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stubs **fail loud**: message to stderr naming the tracking issue, exit code `3`. Never exit 0. | User (Danielle/Sage) — M7-02 runs `vault sync` from launchd; a stub that exits 0 makes a nightly job report success while doing nothing |
| 2 | `requires-python = ">=3.12"` | User (Dependency Skeptic) — every verified dep supports it; `linux/amd64` images for M0-11 are mature |
| 3 | **No automatic remote CI.** Checks run on the Mac via pre-commit's `pre-commit` + `pre-push` stages. GitHub Actions exists as one `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow covering Linux + macOS. | User |
| 4 | Command surface is a **contract**: one spec table, stubs registered from it, a test asserting the registered set matches | User (Carl) |
| 5 | Global `--config` / `--dry-run` / `--yes` / `-v` declared on the root callback now | User (Danielle) — retrofitting across 17 signatures at M5-03 is the expensive version |
| 6 | `docs/decisions.md` skeleton created here | User (Nick over Penny) — nine tickets M0-12..M0-20 have ACs writing to it and no ticket owns creating it |
| 7 | No branch protection requiring a remote check | Resolved from #3 — a required check with no automatic CI blocks every push; the `pre-push` hook is the gate instead |
| 8 | gitleaks in pre-commit only, not a separate CI job | User (not selected); consistent with #3 |
| 9 | Import package `vault`, distribution name `photovault` | Nick's recommendation, unanswered — one line in `pyproject.toml`, trivially changed before M9-03 |
| 10 | `scripts/*.py` get ruff lint + format; **excluded** from strict mypy | Tara's recommendation, unanswered — one-shot tooling, not product code |
| 11 | `verify` is a single stub now; M5-02 and M6-02 add subcommands under it later | Nick's recommendation, unanswered |

## Approach

A single-package `src/` layout with **one** CLI module. The 17 command names, their help
panels, and their tracking issue numbers live in one spec table; stubs are registered from
that table in a loop, so the table is the single source of truth by construction rather than
by convention. A test asserts the registered command set equals the table, which is what
makes AC #1 survive contact with the next 86 tickets.

Strict mypy and a deliberate ruff rule set go on now while there are ~150 lines to satisfy.
`osxphotos` is not added by this ticket, but the dependency structure that keeps it out of
Linux resolution is — that trap otherwise springs at M1-04, in a different ticket than the
mistake.

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`
- **What**: `uv init` shaped into a `src/` layout. `[project]` with `name = "photovault"`,
  `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, `dependencies = ["typer>=0.27,<1.0"]`.
  `[project.scripts] vault = "vault.cli:app"` — verified that `typer.Typer` defines
  `__call__`, so the app object works directly as an entry point.
  `[dependency-groups] dev = ["mypy", "pytest", "ruff", "pre-commit"]` (PEP 735, uv-native).
  Commit `uv.lock`.
- **Why**: Decision 2, 9. Typer is pinned below 1.0 because it is pre-release and has
  recently **dropped its `click` dependency** (verified: a fresh 0.27.2 install pulls `rich`,
  `shellingham`, `annotated-doc` and no click) — anything written against click internals
  will break.
- **Note for later**: when M1-04 adds `osxphotos`, it must carry a marker
  (`osxphotos>=0.76; sys_platform == "darwin"`) or live in a `macos` extra. uv produces a
  **universal** lockfile across platforms, so a bare entry will make resolution attempt
  `pyobjc` on `linux/amd64` and break M0-11's image. Leave a comment in `pyproject.toml`
  saying so.
- **Files**: `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.python-version`

### Step 2: `src/vault/` package
- **What**:
  - `__init__.py` — `__version__` only.
  - `errors.py` — `ExitCode(IntEnum)` with at minimum `OK = 0`, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED = 3`; and a
    `VaultError` base exception.
  - `cli.py` — the whole CLI (see Step 3).
  - `__main__.py` — `from vault.cli import app` / `app()`, so `python -m vault` works. M0-11's
    container will want this.
- **Why**: Penny — 17 stubs are three lines each; one module until they have bodies.
- **Files**: `src/vault/{__init__,errors,cli,__main__}.py`

### Step 3: The command surface
- **What**: In `cli.py`, a module-level spec table — one row per command carrying
  `(name, panel, issue_number, help_text)`. Register stubs from it in a loop via
  `app.command(name=..., rich_help_panel=..., help=...)`. Verified against typer 0.27.2 that
  `rich_help_panel` exists on both `Typer.command()` and `Typer.add_typer()`, and that
  `Typer(no_args_is_help=True)` is supported.

  The 17 commands, each traced to the issue that will implement it:

  | Panel | Commands (issue #) |
  |---|---|
  | **Pipeline** | `ingest` (36) · `fingerprint` (45) · `group` (50) · `select` (52) · `proxy` (59) · `review` (61) · `publish` (68) · `backup` (77) · `sync` (81) |
  | **Safety** | `verify` (69) · `retire` (70) · `scrub` (78) · `restore` (79) |
  | **Operations** | `status` (84) · `rebuild` (21) · `report` (60) · `config` (17) |

  Every stub writes to stderr and raises `typer.Exit(ExitCode.NOT_IMPLEMENTED)`:
  ```
  vault: `ingest` is not implemented yet
         tracked in https://github.com/stephenkiers/PhotoLibrary/issues/36
  ```
  `retire` additionally refuses without `--yes` — the guardrail predates the destructive code
  it will guard (M5-03 deletes originals from Photos by UUID; M0-01 says *"no unattended runs
  against Photos, ever"*).
- **Why**: Derived from `issues.json`'s `flow` block plus per-issue ACs, not invented.
  Issue numbers verified against `.github-issue-map.json`. Flat namespace keeps
  `vault sync` and `docker run vault status` (M0-11's AC) short; `rich_help_panel` supplies
  the legibility that nesting would.
- **Migration path**: when a command gets a real body, delete its row from the stub table and
  write a normal decorated function. The Step 5 test catches either half being forgotten.
- **Files**: `src/vault/cli.py`

### Step 4: Global options on the root callback
- **What**: `@app.callback()` declaring `--config PATH`, `--dry-run`, `--yes/-y`,
  `--verbose/-v` (countable), stored on a frozen dataclass assigned to `ctx.obj`.
  `Typer(no_args_is_help=True)` so bare `vault` prints help.
  **All annotations use `Annotated[T, typer.Option(...)]`** — the legacy
  `x: Path = typer.Option(...)` form assigns an `OptionInfo` to a `Path`-annotated parameter
  and strict mypy rejects it. Establishing this in the root callback sets the pattern for
  every later command.
- **Why**: Decision 5 (Danielle); the `Annotated` constraint is Tara's, and is a hard
  prerequisite for Step 6.
- **Files**: `src/vault/cli.py`

### Step 5: Tests
- **What**: `tests/test_cli.py` using `typer.testing.CliRunner`:
  1. `test_command_surface` — the set of registered command names equals the spec table.
     This is the AC-#1 contract.
  2. `test_help_exits_zero` — `--help` exits 0 and every command name appears in the output.
  3. `test_stub_exits_nonzero` — a representative stub exits `3` and writes its issue URL to
     stderr.
  4. `test_retire_requires_yes` — `retire` without `--yes` fails.
- **Why**: Decision 4. Without #1, AC #1 is a one-time manual check on one Mac; the first
  thing to break is M0-11's `docker run vault status`, which is a *different ticket's*
  acceptance criterion depending on a name nobody pinned.
- **Files**: `tests/test_cli.py`

### Step 6: Lint and type config
- **What**: In `pyproject.toml`:
  - `[tool.ruff]` targeting py312, `select = ["E","F","I","UP","B","SIM","RUF","ANN","TID"]`,
    ruff-format (not black).
  - `[tool.mypy]` `strict = true`, `warn_unreachable = true`,
    `enable_error_code = ["redundant-expr","possibly-undefined","truthy-bool"]`,
    `files = ["src","tests"]`.
  - `scripts/` excluded from mypy; ruff still lints and formats it (Decision 10 — expect a
    mechanical reformat commit of `gen_issues.py` and `push_issues_to_github.py`).
- **Why**: Tara — strict is nearly free on ~150 lines and costs a week at M0-09 (SQLite
  catalog, an "L"). `ANN` catches missing annotations at lint time before mypy runs.
- **Files**: `pyproject.toml`

### Step 7: pre-commit — the actual gate
- **What**: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with
  `default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, pre-push]`:
  - **pre-commit stage** (fast): `ruff check --fix`, `ruff format`, `gitleaks`,
    `check-added-large-files`, `check-merge-conflict`, `end-of-file-fixer`,
    `trailing-whitespace`.
  - **pre-push stage** (slower): `mypy`, `pytest`.

  ruff and mypy hooks use `language: system` invoking `uv run ruff` / `uv run mypy` rather
  than pre-commit's own isolated environments — otherwise the hook rev and the dev-dependency
  pin drift and local disagrees with everything else.
- **Why**: Decision 3 — this *is* AC #2. `check-added-large-files` matters more than usual
  here: this repo will sit next to a multi-terabyte archive.
- **Files**: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

### Step 8: `.gitignore`
- **What**: `vault.toml` (the real config; M0-05 commits `vault.example.toml` instead),
  `.env`, `*.db`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm`, `*.jsonl`, `staging/`, `archive/`, `proxies/`,
  `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `.pytest_cache/`.
- **Why**: Sage — public repo, and M0-05 routes secrets through env/keychain explicitly.
  Excluding the real config before anyone creates one is the only cheap moment to do it.
- **Files**: `.gitignore`

### Step 9: Manual-dispatch workflow
- **What**: `.github/workflows/checks.yml` — `on: workflow_dispatch:` **only**, matrix over
  `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`, running `uv sync`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`,
  `mypy`, `pytest`. Top-level `permissions: contents: read`; `astral-sh/setup-uv` pinned to a
  commit SHA.
- **Why**: Decision 3. The Linux leg is the only thing that will exercise M0-11's target
  platform before the NAS does — run it by hand (`gh workflow run checks.yml`) whenever a
  dependency changes.
- **Files**: `.github/workflows/checks.yml`

### Step 10: `docs/decisions.md` and `README.md`
- **What**: `docs/decisions.md` with a stub heading per open decision ticket (M0-12 … M0-20),
  each naming its issue number and the ticket that consumes the answer. `README.md`: what the
  project is, `uv sync` / `uv run vault --help`, `pre-commit install`. No personal paths
  (M9-02).
- **Why**: Decision 6. Nine ACs currently point at a file no ticket owns.
- **Files**: `docs/decisions.md`, `README.md`

## Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| `osxphotos` breaks the universal lock at M1-04, surfacing as an M0-11 Docker failure | Comment in `pyproject.toml` recording the marker requirement (Step 1) |
| Strict mypy at M0-09 is a wall if adopted late | Adopted now, at ~150 lines (Step 6) |
| Command surface drifts and `docker run vault status` breaks silently | `test_command_surface` (Step 5) |
| A stub silently "succeeds" under launchd | Exit code 3 on every stub (Step 3) |
| pre-push is skippable with `--no-verify` | **Unmitigated and accepted** — there is no automatic remote CI by choice (Decision 3). The `workflow_dispatch` run is the manual fallback |
| `scripts/` reformat noise mixed into the bootstrap commit | Land the ruff reformat of `scripts/` as its own commit |

## Testing Strategy

End-to-end, from a clean clone:

```
uv sync                                # resolves, writes .venv
uv run vault --help                    # AC #1: 17 commands, 3 panels, exit 0
uv run vault ingest; echo $?           # stderr message + issue URL, exit 3
uv run vault retire; echo $?           # refuses without --yes
uv run vault                           # no args -> help, not silence
uv run pytest                          # surface + help + stub + retire tests
uv run mypy && uv run ruff check .     # both clean
pre-commit install --install-hooks
pre-commit run --all-files             # hygiene + gitleaks pass
git commit && git push                 # AC #2: pre-push runs mypy + pytest on the Mac
gh workflow run checks.yml             # manual Linux + macOS verification
```

Negative check that proves the contract holds: add an 18th command without adding it to the
spec table — `test_command_surface` must fail. Then remove a row from the table without
removing the command — it must fail again.

## Out of Scope

| Deferred | Owner |
|---|---|
| Config loading and `vault.example.toml` | M0-05 (#17) — the `config` stub stays a stub |
| Docker image, exiftool/vips/ffmpeg | M0-11 (#23) |
| LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, release workflow | M9-03 (#98) — note the repo is public with no license *today* |
| Full docs | M9-01 (#96) |
| Logging framework, structured output, `--json` | M7-04 (#84) |
| A `doctor` command checking for system binaries | Nobody asked — cut |
| Coverage thresholds | Nobody asked — cut |
| Run-lock / resume conventions (M1-03, M2-04, M3-08, M7-01 each say "resumable") | Raised by Carl, deliberately not reserved here. Flagged so M1-03 sets the convention rather than four tickets each inventing one |
